programme: STAT1, IRF7 and IRF5 form the core STAT1/IRF interferon-response module (STAT1 as the shared signal-transducing hub, IRF7 as the type-I-IFN amplification loop, IRF5 as the pro-inflammatory/M1-like polarization arm) — the same module that drives activation of tissue-resident myeloid cells (microglia, tumor-associated macrophages) toward a phagocytic, cytokine-producing state.
role_in_a: In Alzheimer's disease, STAT1 and IRF5 drive microglial activation directly: STAT1 mediates IL-1β production downstream of Tyro3 signaling and its induction via H3K18 crotonylation causes cognitive deficits, while IRF5 regulates microglial phagocytosis of amyloid pathology. IRF7 sits in the same interferon-stimulated-gene circuit (high Open Targets percentile, shared targets like CXCL10, CCL5, ISG15 with STAT1) but has no disease-specific paper here, so it is inferred as the amplifying arm rather than independently placed.
role_in_b: In papillary kidney carcinoma the same module is expected to operate in tumor-associated macrophages: STAT1 appears in a paper on MARCO+ TAMs impeding CD8+ T cell immunity and driving immunotherapy resistance in renal cell carcinoma, and IRF5 — the canonical driver of pro-inflammatory/M1 macrophage polarization — sits at the 99.96th percentile of Open Targets gene-disease association for this cancer, consistent with a role in shaping the tumor immune microenvironment even though no publication was retrieved for it there.
shared_axis: Both tissues carry a resident myeloid population (microglia in brain, tumor-associated macrophages in kidney) whose activation state is set by the same STAT1/IRF5/IRF7 interferon circuit; in AD this module tips microglia toward a damaging pro-inflammatory phenotype, and in papillary RCC the equivalent module in TAMs determines whether the tumor immune microenvironment is permissive or resistant to immunotherapy — the disease phenotypes differ but the myeloid-activation logic is the same transcriptional wiring redeployed in a different organ.
reasoning: STAT1 and IRF5 are each independently and functionally placed in Alzheimer's disease by direct papers, and each has at least a genetic (IRF5, KIRP percentile 0.9996) or literature (STAT1, TAM/immune-evasion paper) foothold in kidney papillary carcinoma, so the module is nameable and partially anchored in the record. But no retrieved source discusses STAT1/IRF5/IRF7 jointly across both diseases — the myeloid-activation link between brain and kidney tumor is my inference from separately-documented roles, not something retrieved directly, and IRF7 itself has zero disease-specific evidence in either condition.
support: PMID 41206011 (STAT1 mediates IL-1β via Tyro3 signaling in AD microglia); PMID 41676156 (microglial H3K18cr induces STAT1, causing cognitive deficit in AD models); PMID 40968664 (creatine treatment attenuates AD pathology, STAT1-related); PMID 41117057 (STAT1-linked MARCO+ TAMs impede CD8+ T cell immunity and drive immunotherapy resistance in renal cell carcinoma); PMID 38271298 (IRF5 regulates microglial phagocytosis, alleviates AD pathology); PMID 40470298 (IRF5 among senescence-related genes in AD expression analysis); PMID 22685416 (brain eGWAS identifying disease-associated variants, includes IRF5 context).
how_to_falsify: Compare STAT1/IRF5 ChIP-seq or CUT&RUN target occupancy and downstream ISG/cytokine induction (CXCL10, CCL5, IL1B) in microglia from an AD mouse model versus tumor-associated macrophages sorted from papillary RCC patient tumors or xenografts; if STAT1/IRF5 activation in the two myeloid populations does not converge on a shared ISG/pro-inflammatory target signature (e.g., disjoint bound-target sets, opposite cytokine output), the claim that this is one redeployed module rather than coincidental co-recurrence fails. A STAT1 inhibitor (e.g., fludarabine) applied to both an AD microglial activation assay and a papillary RCC TAM co-culture assay should suppress the same class of ISGs in both if the shared-module account is correct.
caveats: Brain and kidney tissues are unrelated anatomically; the claim rests on 112 patient-group comparisons but only 3 independent cohort pairs, so the concordance could reflect shared batch/preprocessing structure rather than independent biological replication. STAT1's support in AD (104/112) is much stronger than IRF7's (83/112) or IRF5's (69/112), and only STAT1 and IRF5 have any disease-specific literature at all — IRF7 is carried by target-overlap and Open Targets percentile alone. RFX5 (MHC-II/antigen-presentation regulator) and STAT4 (another STAT-family immune TF) were both removed as tissue-generic, which is why this account emphasizes the IFN/cytokine-activation arm of the module rather than antigen presentation as the distinguishing signal. No paper places any of these three factors in both diseases jointly, and the papillary-RCC-specific literature is essentially absent for IRF5 and IRF7.
